test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 23 Dec, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct related to eco-system?

(i) UV radiation is not damaging to organisms.

(ii) Ozone at the higher levels of the atmosphere is a product of UV radiation acting on oxygen molecule.

(iii) The amount of ozone in the atmosphere began to drop sharply in 1980.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Only (ii) and (iii)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **UV radiation** is indeed damaging to organisms. It can cause **skin cancer**, **eye damage**, and can also negatively affect **plant life**.
 
• **Ozone** at higher levels of the atmosphere, specifically the **stratosphere**, is produced by UV radiation acting on oxygen molecules, leading to the formation of the **ozone layer** which protects life on Earth by blocking harmful UV radiation.
 
• The amount of ozone in the atmosphere started to drop sharply around **1980** due to the release of **chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs)** and other ozone-depleting substances, leading to the creation of the **ozone hole**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **UV radiation**__

 __
 
• **UV radiation** has both beneficial and harmful effects. While it is crucial for the production of **vitamin D** in humans, excessive exposure can lead to **health issues** such as skin cancer, premature aging, and cataracts.
 
• It also affects marine ecosystems by impacting the survival rates of phytoplankton, which are the foundation of the **marine food web**.
 
 
 
• **Ozone Layer Depletion**__
 
 
• **Ozone layer depletion** is primarily caused by human-made chemicals like **chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs)**, halons, and other related chemicals.
 
• These chemicals release chlorine and bromine atoms in the stratosphere, which destroy ozone molecules.
 
• The **Montreal Protocol**, signed in 1987, is an international treaty designed to phase out the production of numerous substances responsible for ozone depletion.
